sources: Israel Central Elections Committee (via Gulf News citing The Guardian; Asiatoday; Indian Express); Likud statement Oct 28
fault_line: Do 430,000-480,000 double-envelope ballots rescue Netanyahu's bloc -- or just confirm a deadlock that no count can fix?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Election authorities are counting outstanding double-envelope ballots (soldiers, diplomats, prisoners and others) on Thursday after more than 90% of regular votes were tallied, with neither bloc at a majority. The pool is 430,000-480,000 ballots (CEC via Indian Express, carrier undeclared -- attribution only for the pool size); at roughly 40,000 votes per seat that pool could move about 10-12 seats, though it is not expected to change the overall deadlock balance. Likud's Oct 28 allegation that the election was 'stolen by Arab parties' (bribery, threats, violence, forgery, prohibited software) remains UNPROVEN and unverified; the CEC said: 'We have received Likud's request. It is currently under review' (via Asiatoday, carrier undeclared -- attribution only). Final tally expected Thursday evening/Friday; official results Nov 4; Herzog consults factions thereafter and the formateur gets up to 42 days.
sections.what_verified: 1 declared family: The Guardian T2 (via Gulf News liveblog) for the count-under-way Thursday fact. Indian Express and Asiatoday are UNDECLARED in the registry and do not count toward corroboration; their figures are carried with attribution only. Gate note: sig 2, so the sig>=3 two-family gate does not apply; the item passes as an attributed process report, not as a verified final result.
sections.what_disputed: Prior scan 1000-06 flagged a morning republication cluster (85.6-89.8%) that differs from the standing Petek tracker figure 98.17% -- the regular-ballot percentage basis is unresolved; do NOT merge the 90%+ regular-ballot figure with the 98.17% tracker figure. In the previous election double-envelope votes favoured Netanyahu and allies (per Daily Jagran, undeclared -- attribution only), so the pool's direction is not neutral history, but no 2026 double-envelope split is published yet.
sections.why_matters: The count is not over: up to 480,000 double-envelope ballots are being opened Thursday, worth roughly 10-12 seats -- while Likud's 'stolen election' claim sits unproven under committee review.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to Israel election count -- double-envelope ballot count under way Thursday; Likud 'stolen election' allegation under Central Elections Committee review (unproven)
